textbookText: [Fig. 15.6, Real and apparent depth] When an object is viewed from a rarer medium while submerged in a denser medium, it appears shallower than its actual depth. The actual depth is termed as the real depth whereas the perceived depth to the eye is known as the apparent depth.

Hence, the real depth is the actual depth of the object placed in a denser medium and the apparent depth is the virtual depth that is observed as a result of the refraction of light. The apparent depth depends upon the refractive index of the medium.
Consider, a point object O placed at the depth R (=AO) below the surface of a transparent but denser medium like water or glass.
For vertical observation, there is no normal shifting, and no case of apparent depth or shifting of the image.

For oblique observation as in figure 15.6, incident ray OB appears to meet with OA at point I after refraction on the interface. Therefore, I is the virtual image of object O. So AI = a is apparent depth and OI = d is apparent shift (normal shift).
